### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, touching **3** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-version-tokens.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**3** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/data-engine.mdx`  _(via updateData (symbol, a method of class ObjectStackProtocolImplementation))_
- `content/docs/kernel/services-checklist.mdx`  _(via updateData (symbol, a method of class ObjectStackProtocolImplementation))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-version-tokens.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `updateData (4 routes)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 01386412b8a502e823f0f8a3e66c713739cebd05` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `75cd2de3c1979da0d96efccdb290685f8cc2cd95` — the merge of head `00f922f695baf5ea9d865d5ec6359c3d2547f7c8` into base `01386412b8a502e823f0f8a3e66c713739cebd05`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 75cd2de3c1979da0d96efccdb290685f8cc2cd95 && git checkout 75cd2de3c1979da0d96efccdb290685f8cc2cd95
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 01386412b8a502e823f0f8a3e66c713739cebd05 00f922f695baf5ea9d865d5ec6359c3d2547f7c8 && git checkout -B drift-repro 01386412b8a502e823f0f8a3e66c713739cebd05 && git merge --no-ff 00f922f695baf5ea9d865d5ec6359c3d2547f7c8

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 01386412b8a502e823f0f8a3e66c713739cebd05
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 01386412b8a502e823f0f8a3e66c713739cebd05` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `90a6068ffc3d3f0d6cfffe10beb21cbc08de00a9`
Local-runs: none
Scope: no `reviewFace` hits — the eight paths decide no face (no published schema, no governed path; the changeset reads `Clause-②: no`, not the narrowing arm), so the review is the one ruling 5985885287 asks for on the write-door existence boundary ("at-tier contract review before landing"), served at the dispatched tier + packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-record-reads.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts (updateData, deleteData, probeRecord, assertVersionOf, assertVersionMatch, readAsCaller), packages/types/src/data-error-classification.ts (declaredHttpStatus), packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts (steps 2 and 2.7), packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts (callerCannotReadAddressedRow, absentUnderCallerRead, readUnlessRefused), packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/permission-evaluator.ts, packages/spec/src/security/permission.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/api/batch.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts, packages/rest/src/crud-routes.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/data.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.by-id-write-unreadable-row-not-found.ts, content/docs/protocol/kernel/http-protocol.mdx, .changeset/harden-occ-unreadable-row-write-door.md, the four test files of the diff.

Read-only shape held: the diff at this head (`git diff origin/main...FETCH_HEAD`), ruling 5985885287 on #21771, the #28615 body, the head's check runs (50 runs: 49 success, 1 skipped `UI Published Artifacts`), nothing built or run.

### ① Derived judgments

The one changed body is `assertVersionOf`'s mismatch branch (protocol-record-reads.ts :247-259). Reached only from `assertVersionMatch`, whose two callers are `updateData` (protocol.ts :14454) and `deleteData` (:14571), only when the caller sent a token that normalises non-null, the system probe found a row, and the tokens disagree. Each accept-set and public-face change that follows, judged:

1. **Stale token, caller's read returns no row** — was `404 RECORD_NOT_FOUND` minted by the comparison; now the write door's answer. For a caller the write door refuses first (no update/delete grant, the RBAC administration gate): `404` → `403`, refusal to refusal — the ruling's intended consequence, and what the hidden-row rows of both dogfood files and the runtime `READONLY` object measure. For a caller the write door admits up to its read question: the security layer's step 2.7 re-reads as the caller, `absentUnderCallerRead` answers `true` for an absent row, `recordNotFoundError` — `404` → `404`, now produced by the write door (dogfood `showcase_private_note`, PATCH 404). **Correct**, and exactly ruling A's text.

2. **Stale token, caller's read REFUSES (declared 4xx)** — was the read refusal rethrown; now the write door's answer. ⛔ **This arm is not a refusal swap on every path: on one it is refuse → accept, and the accept is a stale write landing.** The class and the positions:
   - a principal holding the object's edit (or delete) grant **without** its read grant. The model admits it: `permission.zod.ts` :263-267 derives `allowRead` and `allowEdit` independently (only `modifyAllRecords` implies both); `permission-evaluator.ts` :53-61 maps `update → allowEdit`, `delete → allowDelete`, `findOne → allowRead`, with no implication between them;
   - on a by-id write where **no write-class row filter binds** — `computeRlsFilter` is declared `Record | null` (security-plugin.ts), and with it null `writeParts.length === 0` at the middleware's step 2.7, so the branch taken is the `else if` at security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts :1146-1156: `callerCannotReadAddressedRow` → `absentUnderCallerRead` → `readUnlessRefused`, which classes a declared 4xx as `refused` and `absentUnderCallerRead` then answers `false` — in the security layer's own words (security-plugin.ts :754-772, :3938-3950): "a declared 4xx refusal — the read itself was REFUSED (the object's read grant withheld…). Not a hidden row, so `false`: the write keeps the answer it has today." Today's answer on that path is admission: no later by-id gate asks the read question again.
   - Both sides read the same predicate (`declaredHttpStatus(e)` defined and below 500: `isCallerReadRefusal` in the diff, `readUnlessRefused` in the security layer), so **every** read the comparison hands over as a refusal is one the write door also declines to treat as absence.
   - Net: before this diff, that principal's stale-token write answered the read door's `403` and the row stayed; at this head it lands. OCC is a no-op for the class. The token "never lets a write land that the same request without a token would not" (true — the no-token write lands there too), but OCC's own promise — a stale token never lands — is what the arm gives up.
   - The docblock's warrant for the arm (protocol.ts :14793-14800, "Handing over loses no guard: the write door refuses a by-id write of a row the caller cannot read (the security layer asks the read question ahead of the write and answers `recordNotFoundError`)") holds for **absence** only; for a **refused** read the security layer documents the opposite, as quoted. The changeset's last bullet ("a caller who may write the object gets `404 RECORD_NOT_FOUND` for a row its read does not return") is likewise true of absence only.
   - No pin covers the class: the protocol test's refusing-read case (`protocol.record-not-found.test.ts` :429-444) pairs every refusal with `refuse: 'u1'`, so the write is always refused and the admitted half is never measured; the runtime `READONLY` object is read-without-write (the mirror image); every dogfood principal holds read on the objects it aims at. The ablation therefore could not have gone red on this class either.

3. **Readable row, including readable-not-writable** — `409 CONCURRENT_UPDATE` with `currentRecord` as the caller reads it. Unchanged; pinned (runtime `READABLE_ID` on `READONLY`, dogfood `showcase_account` for the plain member, wall test rows of B). **Correct**, and the right call against option a′.

4. **Read faults** (server-band status, or none declared) propagate; the write is never asked. Unchanged; pinned (bare `Error`, `503`). **Correct.**

5. **Token agrees, or none sent** — no caller read is issued (`if (!expected) return`, `versionTokensAgree` short-circuit): unchanged bytes. **Correct.**

6. **Token on an id naming no row** — `assertVersionMatch`'s system probe returns null, `assertVersionOf` returns at `if (!current) return`, the write door answers. Unchanged; it is the "hit equals miss" anchor every new pin compares against. **Correct.**

7. **Non-authorization 4xx on the re-read** (a `400` on a malformed id, a `422`, a `429`) — `isCallerReadRefusal` hands these over too. Because the write then runs the exact path the no-token request runs, no accept the no-token request lacks is created; but on the admit path the token is dropped silently, the same shape as item 2 one class narrower. Folded into the must-fix: whichever route closes item 2 decides this predicate.

8. **Bulk faces carry no token — verified.** `BatchRecordSchema` (batch.zod.ts :49-53: `id`, `data`, `externalId`), `UpdateManyRecordSchema` / `UpdateManyRequestSchema` (no `expectedVersion`, no `version`), `UpdateManyDataRequestSchema` extends it with `object` only (protocol.zod.ts :3248); `assertVersionMatch` has exactly the two by-id callers above; the REST `If-Match` readers are crud-routes.ts :411 (PATCH by id) and :523 (DELETE by id) and the dispatcher's data.ts :62-63 (by id). Nothing to align. **Claim holds.**

9. **Public faces.** No published schema changes; no governed path; `ConcurrentUpdateError`'s shape unchanged; the `MalformedVersionTokenError` 400 still runs ahead of every read (`assertVersionTokenNotMalformed` first in both functions). The http-protocol.mdx paragraph (:724-727) states the code as written — "for any other id it gets exactly what the same request without a token gets" — which on the refused-read admit path is a landed write, so the sentence is accurate and the behaviour it describes is the defect.

10. **Precedent.** #28615 (`Clause-②: no`, patch) was a refusal order swap with no accept-set change. Items 1, 3-6, 8 are in that class. Item 2 is not.

### ② Semver level

Declared: `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` patch, `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`. **Not right for the diff at this head**: item 2 moves a request from the refuse set to the accept set (a stale-token by-id write by an edit-without-read principal on a floor-less object lands), so `Clause-②: no` as a plain refusal-swap declaration does not hold. With the refusal arm closed by either route in ④, the remaining change is a refusal swap on existing doors and the declaration and level are right, on the #28615 precedent. The `Metadata-protocol: none` line is right either way (no schema, no wire shape).

### ③ Boundary flags

- Author `objectstack-fleet[bot]`: no login note owed.
- `open_questions` / flags in the body, each answered:
  - **rest `dist` bundling observation (carrier none):** read; no action — the bundled bytes change with the package they come from, and the changeset convention cited is the prevailing one. Not a must-fix.
  - **NOT MEASURED locally (`check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `spec check:skill-examples`, `check:type-check-debt`):** covered by CI on this head — `Build Core`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger` all success (50 check runs, 49 success, 1 skipped `UI Published Artifacts`, none failed, none pending).
  - **Full dogfood battery not run locally; the seat runs the four token-carrying files:** adequate for the regression question. The changed branch is reachable only through a by-id write carrying a non-empty token (item 5), so a dogfood file that sends none traverses unchanged bytes; `git grep` of `packages/qa/dogfood/test` for `If-Match` / `expectedVersion` at this head names exactly four files — `data-request-shape-live`, `object-designer-field-reorder` (the meta door's `If-Match`, an untouched path), `occ-stale-token-organization-wall`, `update-by-id-refusal-order` — and the head's `Dogfood Regression Gate` is success. ⛔ Adequacy for coverage of the must-fix class is a separate matter: no dogfood principal is in it (item 2), so running the four files proves nothing about it.
  - **Option a′ ruled out (readable-not-writable keeps 409):** implemented and pinned; agreed.
- **Flag raised here, not by the dev:** the maintainer's option (a) was taken on the premise "no guard is lost" (PR body, docblock). The premise is false for one principal class (item 2). The maintainer should see item 2 before the refusal arm lands in any form — ④ names the two routes, and the choice between them is a ruling, not a dev call.

### ④ Design judgment

No `hits` file; the face judged is the ruling's security boundary — the diff against ruling 5985885287 and against the code it cites.

- **The absence arm** (item 1) is ruling A verbatim: "a row the caller cannot read answers exactly what a nonexistent id answers, on update and delete alike. This is the read door's answer." The comparison stops minting a `404` of its own in front of authorization, and the write door — whose step 2.7 now asks the read question for every principal (migration entry 18) — answers for hidden and missing alike. Reading of `assertVersionMatch` → `probeRecord` (system) → `assertVersionOf` → `readAsCaller` (caller context) → return → `engine.update` / `engine.delete` confirms the order the docblocks describe. **Holds.**

- **The refusal arm** (item 2) exceeds the ruling and contradicts OCC. The ruling governs what the write doors answer for a row the caller cannot read; it says nothing that licenses a stale token to land, and its own execution note is the opposite instinct ("an operator who needs a user to write a row grants that user read access to it first" — migration entry 18, acceptance criterion). The security layer deliberately keeps a *refused* read as "today's answer" (#21771's execution; #22851 ruling C kept that notion for the write path on purpose), and today's answer on the floor-less by-id path is admission. Handing over there turns OCC into a no-op for the class. **Must-fix.** Two routes, neither a dev call alone:
  - **(i) Narrow the handover to absence.** Hand over only when `readAsCaller` *returns* null; a declared-4xx read refusal is rethrown, as before this diff (`isCallerReadRefusal` then goes). Consequence to weigh: for a caller holding **neither** grant on the object, a stale token on an existing row answers the read door's `403` and on a missing id the write door's `403` — same status and code (`PERMISSION_DENIED`, both from `PermissionDeniedError`), but the two sentences can differ (the ablation's "equal status and code, different sentence" reading is this residue). That sentence-level difference is a sliver of the oracle the refusal arm set out to close, so it needs the maintainer's acceptance, or a sentence alignment at the read door's object-level refusal, which is another door.
  - **(ii) Close the gap at the write door.** Make step 2.7's addressed by-id arm treat a *refused* caller read as "cannot read" (as `unreadableUnderCallerRead` already does for the explain door under #22851 ruling C), so the handover is safe for every class. That is a no-token accept→refuse flip for the edit-without-read class on floor-less objects — `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` territory in `plugin-security`, outside this PR's declared scope and against #21771's explicit "a refusal keeps today's answer". A ruling, with its own card.
  - Either way: a pin for the class — a principal granted edit (and delete) without read on an object with no write-class row filter, a stale token on an existing row: the row must be unchanged after the call, on update and on delete, at the protocol double (`refuse` unset, `readRefusal` set, assert `update`/`del` not called or the store unchanged) and at one real door.

- **Docblocks / changeset / docs**, judged against the code: protocol.ts :14778-14810 and the record-reads header are accurate on absence, faults, readable rows and the bulk faces; the "Handing over loses no guard" paragraph (:14793-14800) and the changeset's last bullet are false for a refused read and must say what the security layer does with one, or go with the arm. The http-protocol.mdx paragraph needs no change under route (i) or (ii) as written ("answered 409 only for a record the caller can read; for any other id… what the same request without a token gets").

- **Pins otherwise non-vacuous:** the ablation evidence in the body (6/4/2 failures, restore proven, counts 28/20/21) matches the cases I read: the protocol cases compare status, code and sentence across hit, miss and no-token; the runtime `READONLY` object measures both doors and both verbs with the body compared whole; both dogfood files compare the whole answer across three carriers and hold the row image before/after; the controls (409 carrying the row, current token updates 200, the wall real and the member no platform admin) keep a green run from meaning "every token is ignored". The one gap is the class named in item 2.

**Must-fix**
- M1 (item 2, ④): the refused-read arm of the handover lets a stale by-id write land for an edit-without-read principal where no write-class row filter binds (`assertVersionOf` :255-258 → middleware :1146-1156 → `absentUnderCallerRead` false on `refused`). Take route (i) or obtain the ruling for (ii); add the class pin; correct the "loses no guard" docblock paragraph and the changeset bullet. Until then `Clause-②: no` does not describe the diff.

**Should-fix**
- S1: if any refusal arm survives, `isCallerReadRefusal` should name the read door's refusal statuses rather than every client-band status (item 7); a `400`/`422`/`429` on the re-read is not a verdict about the caller.
- S2: the protocol double's refusing-read case should run once with `refuse` unset so the admitted half is measured, not only the refused half.
- S3: the seat's four-file dogfood narrowing is adequate for regression (③) and should be recorded as the measured set on the hand-off, with the note that it does not reach the M1 class.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `8372e0a15d5871e41ad25c8361f7168e4639fb12`
Local-runs: none
Scope: delta review by the same reviewer as record 6561342764 (FAIL on `90a6068ff`), scoped to the rework commit `8372e0a15` on top of merge `357b2bac2` — no `reviewFace` hits, as before (the paths decide no face; review owed by ruling 5985885287's at-tier clause) + packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-record-reads.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts (ConcurrentUpdateError, updateData, probeRecord, assertVersionOf docblocks), .changeset/harden-occ-unreadable-row-write-door.md, content/docs/protocol/kernel/http-protocol.mdx, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.record-not-found.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/data-conflict-caller-visibility.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/update-by-id-refusal-order.dogfood.test.ts; read for the trace, unchanged: packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts (step 2.7), packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts (absentUnderCallerRead, readUnlessRefused).

Read-only shape held: `git diff 357b2bac2..8372e0a15`, the merge verified, the PR body at this head, the head's check runs; nothing built or run.

**Merge claim verified.** `git diff c16040d8d..90a6068ff` (the PR before the merge) and `git diff c2a5be03b..357b2bac2` (the PR after it) are identical apart from hunk line offsets (`http-protocol.mdx` moved by 32 lines, `protocol.ts` by 126–314 lines): the merge's own changes touch none of the diff's lines. The delta below is therefore exactly `357b2bac2..8372e0a15` (7 files, +158/−109).

### ① Derived judgments

1. **M1 closed — only a returned no-row hands over.** `assertVersionOf` (protocol-record-reads.ts :240-242) now reads `const visible = await this.readAsCaller(object, id, context); if (!visible) return;` with no `try`/`catch`; `isCallerReadRefusal` and the `declaredHttpStatus` import are gone (the file no longer imports from `@objectstack/types`). Every throw from `readAsCaller` propagates to the caller of `updateData`/`deleteData` before `engine.update`/`engine.delete` is reached. Trace for the M1 class (edit/delete grant without read, no write-class row filter): the read door's `PermissionDeniedError` 403 is raised by `assertVersionOf`, `assertVersionMatch` does not resolve, `updateData` :14757 / `deleteData` never reach the engine; the security layer's step 2.7 `else if` arm (middleware :1146-1156, `absentUnderCallerRead` false on `refused`) is never asked. **No path remains on which a refused read reaches the write door with a token**: the only `return` on the mismatch branch is the `!visible` one, and `readAsCaller` is `engine.findOne` under the caller's context, which returns `null` for absent/hidden and throws for refused — the same two-way split the write door reads (`readUnlessRefused`). The runtime pin's no-token control landing `200` on `WRITEONLY` through the real security layer confirms the class was reachable, i.e. the FAIL was not hypothetical.
